# The client

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference.py from the docstrings of the lakana package. Do not edit by hand:
run `uv run python scripts/generate_reference.py` and commit the result. -->

The Lakana SDK's entry point.

Signature: `lakana.Client(url: str | None = None, token: str | None = None, *, profile: str | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0, verify: bool | str = True, http_client: httpx.Client | None = None)`

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `str | None` | `None` | The platform API's base URL, given together with `token`. When both are omitted, the client reads `LAKANA_URL` and `LAKANA_TOKEN` (set both or neither), then the profile in `~/.config/lakana/config.toml` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lakana/config.toml` when that variable is set). |
| `token` | `str | None` | `None` | A PAT or task token. |
| `profile` | `str | None` | `None` | A named profile to select from the profile file, when `url`/`token` are not given explicitly and no `LAKANA_URL`/`LAKANA_TOKEN` are set. |
| `timeout` | `float` | `30.0` | Request timeout in seconds. |
| `verify` | `bool | str` | `True` | TLS verification setting: `True` (the default), `False`, or a CA bundle path. |
| `http_client` | `httpx.Client | None` | `None` | An existing `httpx.Client` to use instead of building one — for example in tests, or Starlette's `TestClient`. |

Each resource of the client has its page in the [Python SDK reference](index.md).

## `lakana.Client.from_ci_oidc`

Signature: `lakana.Client.from_ci_oidc(url: str, *, environment: str, repository: str, provider: Literal['github', 'gitlab'] | None = None, id_token: str | None = None, audience: str | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0, verify: bool | str = True, http_client: httpx.Client | None = None) -> Client`

Build a client for a CI job from its OIDC ID token, without a stored secret.

The job's ID token is exchanged for a CI token (``lakana_ci_…``) that may queue one deploy of the job's own commit, or one dry run, of `repository` to `environment`, and then follow that run. Each client needs a new exchange: build one per submission. The ID token and the CI token stay in memory; neither is written, logged or shown.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `str` | required | The Lakana server's base URL. |
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment the job deploys to. |
| `repository` | `str` | required | The registered repository it deploys. |
| `provider` | `Literal['github', 'gitlab'] | None` | `None` | ``github`` asks the GitHub Actions runner for a new ID token (the job needs ``permissions: id-token: write``); ``gitlab`` reads ``LAKANA_OIDC_TOKEN``, which the job's ``id_tokens:`` entry sets. `None` reads ``LAKANA_OIDC``, and without it takes the ID token from ``LAKANA_OIDC_TOKEN``. |
| `id_token` | `str | None` | `None` | The ID token itself; wins over `provider`. |
| `audience` | `str | None` | `None` | The audience to ask GitHub for: the server's ``LAKANA_CI_OIDC__AUDIENCE``. By default ``LAKANA_OIDC_AUDIENCE``, and without it `url` exactly as given. |
| `timeout` | `float` | `30.0` | Request timeout in seconds. |
| `verify` | `bool | str` | `True` | TLS verification for the Lakana server: `True`, `False` or a CA bundle path. |
| `http_client` | `httpx.Client | None` | `None` | An existing `httpx.Client` to send through, for example in tests. |

Returns: `Client`. A client authenticated with the CI token; `ci_token` describes it.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ConfigError` | If no ID token can be found; the message names the variable or permission to add. |
| `lakana.AuthenticationError` | If the provider or the server refuses the ID token; the message says why. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If no single enabled CI trust rule accepts it for this environment and repository. |

## `client.url`

Read-only attribute: `str`

The platform base URL this client talks to.

## `client.sql`

Signature: `client.sql(sql: str, environment: str, timeout: float | None = None, *, into: str | None = None, mode: str | None = None, incremental_key: str | None = None, evolve_schema: bool = False, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> pa.Table | QueryStatus`

Submit a query, wait for it to finish, and return its result or its write status.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sql` | `str` | required | The SQL text to run. |
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment to run the query against. |
| `timeout` | `float | None` | `None` | Seconds to wait before giving up, or `None` to wait indefinitely. Passed straight through to `QueryRun.wait`. |
| `into` | `str | None` | `None` | Write the result into this table or view instead. |
| `mode` | `str | None` | `None` | `create`, `replace`, `append` or `view`; required with `into`. |
| `incremental_key` | `str | None` | `None` | With `mode="append"`, append only rows past the target's maximum of this column. |
| `evolve_schema` | `bool` | `False` | With `replace`/`append`, let the target adopt the result's schema. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |

Returns: `pa.Table or QueryStatus`. The result, or — with `into` — the finished run's status, which carries `rows_written`, `snapshot_id`, `watermark` and `schema_diff` (a write has no result set).

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.QueryFailed` | If the query fails. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the write options don't go together. |
| `TimeoutError` | If `timeout` elapses before the query finishes. |

## `client.whoami`

Signature: `client.whoami() -> Whoami`

Describe who this client's credential authenticates as.

Returns: `Whoami`. The principal's name and type, and its scope if the credential is a task token or a CI token.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.AuthenticationError` | If the credential is invalid, expired or revoked. |

## `client.set_language`

Signature: `client.set_language(language: str | None) -> Whoami`

Set the language you see catalog texts in, or remove it with `None`.

Tables and columns then show their labels and descriptions in it where the project or an edit has them, unless a call asks for another (`lang=`). A task or CI token may not set one.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | `str | None` | required | A language tag such as `"de"` or `"fr-CH"`, any case; `None` removes it. |

Returns: `Whoami`. Who you are, with the language now stored, in its canonical spelling.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | For a task or CI token. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `language` is not a language tag. |

## `client.search`

Signature: `client.search(environment: str, q: str, *, kind: Literal['table', 'column', 'run', 'principal', 'term'] | None = None, model_kind: Literal['fact', 'dimension', 'wide', 'staging'] | None = None, limit: int = 20, offset: int = 0, lang: str | None = None) -> SearchPage`

Find tables, columns, labels, descriptions, runs, principals and terms by a text.

Matching ignores case and finds the text anywhere in a name, label or description. Exact matches come first, then names and labels that start with the text, then names and labels that contain it, then descriptions and declared grains; within each, tables come before columns, runs, principals and terms. Texts in a table's main language always match; translated texts match in your language, and each hit's ``language`` says which language matched. A table, column or term is one hit, however many of its texts match. You see only what you may read: tables and columns with ``READ_TABLE`` on the table, runs with ``READ_ENVIRONMENT`` (found by the first four or more characters of the id, the job or the repository), principals if you may list them, glossary terms with ``READ_ENVIRONMENT`` (found by their name, synonyms and definition). A table or column a term links is also found by the term's name and synonyms, with ``matched`` ``term`` and the term's key in ``term``, if you may read the environment and the table.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `q` | `str` | required | The text, 1 to 200 characters after trimming. |
| `kind` | `Literal['table', 'column', 'run', 'principal', 'term'] | None` | `None` | Only this kind of hit: ``table``, ``column``, ``run``, ``principal`` or ``term``. |
| `model_kind` | `Literal['fact', 'dimension', 'wide', 'staging'] | None` | `None` | Only tables whose asset header declares this ``kind``: ``fact``, ``dimension``, ``wide`` or ``staging``; other hits are left out. |
| `limit` | `int` | `20` | Hits per page, 1 to 100. |
| `offset` | `int` | `0` | Hits to skip, for the next page. |
| `lang` | `str | None` | `None` | The language to match translated texts in, such as ``de`` or ``fr-CH``; without it, your profile's language, else the instance's main language. |

Returns: `SearchPage`. The page; ``has_more`` says whether to ask again with a larger ``offset``.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the text, ``model_kind``, ``limit`` or ``offset`` is out of range, the message naming the range, or ``lang`` is not a language tag. |

## `client.info`

Signature: `client.info() -> InstanceInfo`

Ask the instance which platform version it runs.

The request is sent once, without the transport's retries, so a dead server fails fast.

Returns: `InstanceInfo`. The instance's version.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.AuthenticationError` | If the credential is invalid, expired or revoked. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the server predates the endpoint. |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | If the URL answers with something that is not Lakana's JSON. |

## `client.status`

Signature: `client.status() -> InstanceStatus`

Ask whether the instance is healthy, degraded or down, and why.

Any signed-in caller may ask. With `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT` on the instance the answer also names every cause and has the detail: busy and total task slots, the workers' memory against their limits, and the workers.

Returns: `InstanceStatus`. The state, the causes the caller may see, the counts of workers and, for an administrator, the detail.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.AuthenticationError` | If the credential is invalid, expired or revoked. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the server predates the endpoint. |

## `client.close`

Signature: `client.close() -> None`

Close the underlying HTTP transport.
